messages:
Lina (Product): thinking about adding a keyboard shortcut to quick-approve scorecard items: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to approve the focused item. want feedback on discoverability and accessibility.

Hari (Designer): mockup: show shortcut hint on hover of Approve button and in the scorecard header help menu. small keycap chip "⌘⏎" next to Approve. also propose a subtle confirmation pattern (toast with undo) vs modal.

Jose (Frontend): impl notes: Cmd+Enter mapping is straightforward. Concern: mobile and Windows: use Ctrl+Enter for Windows, obviously. Also focus management: the shortcut should act on the currently focused scorecard row, not just the last clicked.

Jose (Frontend): for accidental approvals we can do two approaches: a) lightweight toast with "Undo" for 5s b) require holding the shortcut for 300-500ms (hold-to-confirm). Both are doable, toast is less interruptive.

Mei (Accessibility): screen reader concerns: if we do toast with undo, ensure it is announced as status with clear textual context: e.g., "Scorecard: approval submitted for test-suite X. Undo available." Also include role="button" for Undo and ensure keyboard focus lands logically (do NOT autofocus the toast). For hold-to-confirm, ensure there's no race with screen reader key repeat; that tends to be fragile.

Owen (PM): product preference: toast with undo. We want minimal UX friction. But there are business constraints: approvals trigger downstream workflows; accidental approvals are high-cost. Maybe require a lightweight 2-step for first-time approvers per-run: show a short inline confirmation checkbox "I understand this will trigger rollout" the first time they approve this run.

Lina (Product): combining ideas: default quick-approve via Cmd+Enter -> create approval + show undo toast. For users who have not approved before in this project, show a one-time modal with brief copy + "Remember my choice" checkbox. Does that make sense?

Hari (Designer): copy suggestion for modal: "Approve this scorecard? Approving will mark this run as approved and may trigger downstream rollouts. [ ] Remember my choice for this project." Buttons: Confirm (primary), Cancel (secondary). Keep copy short.

Mei (Accessibility): language nits: avoid passive voice; propose: "Approve run 'smoke-test'? Approving will start configured rollouts." For the toast: "Approved 'smoke-test'. Undo" Screen reader: announce exactly once. Also ensure the modal uses aria-modal and focus trap.

Jose (Frontend): keyboard behavior: pressing Cmd+Enter while modal open should confirm. Escape cancels. We'll need to persist "remember my choice" in local storage and backend preference (opt-in) so it works across devices if user expects.

Owen (PM): bulk approve: shortcut should only act on a single focused item. For bulk actions we keep dedicated bulk controls. But we should support selecting multiple rows and then Cmd+Enter acting as bulk confirm if focus is on the bulk toolbar. Clarify in docs.

Lina (Product): acceptance criteria to include in ticket: 1) Cmd/Ctrl+Enter quick-approve wired to focused row; 2) toast undo with 5s undo window, announced via role/status; 3) first-time modal appears once per project, with "remember" option; 4) keyboard shortcuts documented in help menu and hover hint chips; 5) no focus steal on toast; 6) bulk behavior scoped to selection state.

Jose (Frontend): will open PR draft, include automated e2e for shortcut and undo flow. Also include unit tests for first-time modal preference persistence.

Hari (Designer): I'll add hover keycap visuals to the scorecard and design the modal copy with final wording. dropping frames to figma by EOD.

Mei (Accessibility): I'll write the a11y test cases: NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack. Also test keyboard-only flow and screen-reader announcement timing.

release-bot: staging build 789 deployed — e2e shortcut tests passing :white_check_mark:

Lina (Product): thanks all. tagging @Jose @Mei @Hari to link tickets when created. planning to ship toggled off by default with admin flag for orgs.

Owen (PM): add a line in release notes about the new shortcut and the safety modal. make sure compliance knows about possible rollout triggers.

Lina (Product): moving to follow-up board. thanks everyone :)
